second_order: gathering people to make Demo together
theme_note: These turns all try to make a group capable of acting: asking whether enough people exist, offering to join, seeking coordination, tracking threads, or volunteering as a representative. What varies is the venue and role—from the subreddit and Talkhaus to Discord, from pixel placers to a diplomat.

second_order: showing where and what to draw
theme_note: These turns make the proposed object actionable by supplying a goal, coordinates, a community tag, a smaller sprite, an outline, or a final goal. They vary between locating the pixels and changing Demo's visible form.

These turns seek, refuse, condition, verify, or rearrange room among Sweden, GreenLattice, dave/10 and other nearby work. The practice is making the drawing coexist on contested space; it varies from asking permission and checking reports to shrinking Demo, moving a neighbour, or appealing after deletion.

These turns resume placement, praise and defend the standing sprite, diagnose its destruction, and automate replacement pixels. What varies is the means: ordinary placement and watching for vandals versus a moderator-adapted bot script.

second_order: calling the attempt off and back on
theme_note: These turns tell people to stop when work looks futile and then reopen the attempt when Sweden may be helping. The later video-thread edits repeat that uncertainty for visitors, moving from invitation to cancellation to making readers decide for themselves.

second_order: explaining and joking about the canvas
theme_note: These turns answer confusion with a plain April-first explanation or joke about the automated account that appeared. They vary between orienting someone to the event and reacting playfully to a sitewide bot.

second_order: putting the project into the usual video posts
theme_note: The routine ASPE and MegaMari entries stay visible while their edited comments recruit the usual link-following audience into the r/place project. The practice joins ordinary posting to project recruitment; it varies only by series and duplicate wording.

second_order: leaving only an r/place title behind
theme_note: This single code records the one practice visible in a deleted post: publishing an r/place-titled submission. Nothing surviving shows what the author said or did in its body, so it belongs with no fuller practice.

second_order: ending with praise, mourning and thanks
theme_note: These turns make a shared ending out of failure: crediting the hours Demo stood and the solid try, mourning it, saying RIP, thanking players, and affirming the upbeat account. What varies is whether a speaker stresses loss, effort, or gratitude.

second_order: pointing back at Demo in the timelapse
theme_note: Both turns share the finished-event practice of directing people who missed the kerfluffle to Demo in a timelapse. One is the post title and the other explains the purpose to latecomers.
